blocks.text: **Harshavardhana (606–647 CE)** of the **Pushyabhuti dynasty** made **Kanauj** the political centre of north India and was the **last great ancient Hindu emperor of the north**. His reign is richly documented by **Banabhatta's Harshacharita and the Chinese pilgrim Xuanzang (Hiuen Tsang)**.

rows: Defeated by the **Chalukya Pulakeshin II on the Narmada (c. 618-19 CE)** — could not expand into the Deccan.
A Shaiva who turned **Buddhist (Mahayana)**; held grand assemblies at **Kanauj & Prayag (every 5 years)**.
Wrote Sanskrit plays — **Nagananda, Ratnavali, Priyadarshika**; patronised Nalanda.

items: **Hiuen-Tsang** (630–645 CE) visited **Harshavardhana**; his **Si-Yu-Ki** records Nalanda (10,000 students) & Harsha's welfare rule.

Harsha: last great northern emperor; defeated by **Pulakeshin II (Chalukya)** on the Narmada; convened the **Kannauj & Prayag assemblies**; author of **Ratnavali, Priyadarshika, Nagananda**; **Banabhatta** wrote Harshacharita.

**Pushyabhuti (Vardhana) dynasty**, capital shifted **Thaneswar → Kannauj**; Harsha united north India after the Guptas; his defeat by **Pulakeshin II (Chalukya)** on the **Narmada (~618 CE)** checked his southern expansion (recorded in the **Aihole inscription** of Ravikirti).

**Sources**: **Banabhatta's Harshacharita** (biography) & **Kadambari**; **Hiuen-Tsang's Si-Yu-Ki** (visited 630–644, studied at Nalanda under Silabhadra); Harsha's own plays — **Nagananda, Ratnavali, Priyadarshika**.

**Administration**: benevolent, decentralised (like Gupta feudal model); revenue shares — **Bhaga** (crown), grants to officials in land (rise of feudalism); toured his realm; held grand **Kanauj assembly** & the **Prayag (Allahabad) quinquennial assembly** (Mahamoksha Parishad — gave away his wealth).
**Religion**: originally **Shaiva**, became a patron of **Mahayana Buddhism** (influenced by Hiuen-Tsang); tolerant; sent an embassy to **Tang China (641)**.
**Nalanda** flourished under Harsha's patronage; after his death the empire disintegrated (no heir) → the age of **Rajput/regional kingdoms** & the **tripartite struggle** for Kannauj.
Harsha stopped by Pulakeshin II at the Narmada; Banabhatta + Xuanzang are the sources; Kanauj & Prayag assemblies.
Harsha authored Nagananda, Ratnavali, Priyadarshika — a scholar-king.

blocks.text: The **Chalukyas of Badami (Vatapi) (6th–8th CE)** dominated the Deccan, most famously under **Pulakeshin II**, who checked Harsha. They pioneered the **Vesara temple style and rock-cut/structural temples at Badami, Aihole and Pattadakal** — 'the cradle of Indian temple architecture'.

rows: Greatest; defeated **Harsha** (Narmada); **Aihole inscription** by **Ravikirti**; received Persian embassy; defeated by Pallava **Narasimhavarman I** (Vatapi sacked).
**Vesara** style; **Aihole** ('cradle of Indian architecture'), **Pattadakal** (UNESCO), **Badami** cave temples.
Patronised **Hinduism, Jainism & Buddhism**; Vaishnava & Shaiva temples.

sections.heading: 🔎 Exam-ready deep coverage: Chalukyas of Badami (Vatapi)

items: **Badami (Vatapi) Chalukyas (6th–8th c CE)**, capital **Vatapi/Badami**; founder **Pulakeshin I**; greatest **Pulakeshin II** (defeated Harsha; received the Persian embassy — Ajanta painting; defeated by the Pallava **Narasimhavarman I** who took Vatapi, 642).

**Art & architecture** — the **Vesara/Chalukyan** style & **rock-cut + structural** experiments: **Badami cave temples**, **Aihole** ('cradle of Indian temple architecture' — Durga, Lad Khan temples), **Pattadakal** (**UNESCO** — Virupaksha temple by Lokamahadevi, blends Nagara & Dravida).
**Aihole inscription** of **Ravikirti** (court poet, in Sanskrit) records Pulakeshin II's victories; patronage of Hinduism, Jainism & Buddhism.
**Branches**: Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi & later Western (Kalyani) Chalukyas descend from this line.
Pulakeshin II beat Harsha but was defeated by Pallava Narasimhavarman I (Vatapikonda).
Aihole = cradle of Indian temple architecture; Pattadakal = UNESCO; Vesara style.

blocks.text: The **Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi (c. 624–1075 CE)**, founded by **Kubja Vishnuvardhana** (brother of Pulakeshin II), ruled **coastal Andhra for ~four centuries** and were pivotal for **Telugu literature** — patronising **Nannaya**, the Adikavi — before merging with the imperial Cholas.

rows: **Kubja Vishnuvardhana**, brother of Badami Chalukya **Pulakeshin II**; capital **Vengi**.
~400 years — the longest-ruling dynasty of coastal Andhra.
**Rajaraja Narendra** patronised **Nannaya (Adikavi)**, who began the **Telugu Mahabharatam**.
Merged with the **Cholas** via **Kulottunga I** (Chalukya-Chola line).

sections.heading: 🔎 Exam-ready deep coverage: Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi

items: **Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi (624–1130 CE)**, founded by **Kubja Vishnuvardhana** (brother of Pulakeshin II); capital **Vengi/Pishtapura → Rajamahendravaram (Rajahmundry)**; buffer between the **Rashtrakutas & Cholas**.

Ruled coastal Andhra (Godavari-Krishna) for ~5 centuries → key to **Andhra's political & cultural identity**; matrimonial ties with the **Cholas** (Rajaraja Narendra married a Chola princess; his son Kulottunga I united the two thrones).
**Cultural landmark**: under **Rajaraja Narendra (1022–61)**, **Nannaya Bhattaraka** began the **Telugu Mahabharatam** — the **dawn of Telugu literature** (Nannaya = **Adikavi**).
**Temples**: Draksharamam (Bhimeswara — a Pancharama), Biccavolu, Chebrolu — Chalukyan-Dravida blend; religious tolerance (Shaiva, Vaishnava, Jain).
Kubja Vishnuvardhana (Pulakeshin II's brother) founded the Vengi line; capital Vengi.
Rajaraja Narendra → Nannaya → Telugu Mahabharatam is the key Telugu-literature fact.

blocks.text: The **Rashtrakutas (753–982 CE)**, founded by **Dantidurga** with capital **Manyakheta**, were a great **western-Deccan imperial power** engaged in the **'tripartite struggle' for Kanauj**. They are immortalised by the **Kailasa temple at Ellora** and were patrons of **Kannada, Sanskrit and Jainism**.

rows: **Govinda III, Amoghavarsha I** (wrote **Kavirajamarga** in Kannada; **Ratnamalika**; Jain).
**Kailasa temple, Ellora** (rock-cut, Krishna I) — monolithic marvel; Elephanta caves influence.
Arab traveller **Al-Masudi**; praised as one of the four great empires of the world (Sulaiman).

items: **Rashtrakutas (753–982 CE)**, capital **Manyakheta (Malkhed)**; founder **Dantidurga** (overthrew the Badami Chalukyas); greatest — **Govinda III** & **Amoghavarsha I** (wrote the Kannada classic **Kavirajamarga** & Jain **Prashnottara Ratnamalika**; called 'Ashoka of the South').

Central player in the **tripartite struggle** for Kannauj (vs Palas & Pratiharas); powerful, wealthy — the Arab traveller **Al-Masudi** called the Rashtrakuta king one of the four great kings of the world; **Sulaiman** praised their tolerance.

**Art**: the monolithic **Kailasa temple at Ellora (Cave 16)** — carved top-down from a single rock by **Krishna I** — the greatest rock-cut monument in India; **Elephanta** Trimurti (Shiva) cave associated with this age.
Patronised **Kannada, Sanskrit & Jainism**; promoted trade with the Arab world.

blocks.text: Ellora Kailasa (Rashtrakuta) is the exam favourite: **monolithic, top-down carved, Cave 16, Krishna I, dedicated to Shiva**.

items: Dantidurga founder; Amoghavarsha (Kavirajamarga, Kannada); Kailasa temple Ellora (Krishna I).
Tripartite struggle for Kanauj = Rashtrakuta–Pratihara–Pala.
